summary:
### TL;DR
- **Possible workflow breakage:** The GitHub Code Quality `upload-code-coverage` action now fails the upload step if the coverage report is not in Cobertura XML format. Before this change, such uploads appeared to succeed but showed no coverage on pull requests. ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-23-code-coverage-uploads-now-flag-invalid-report-formats))
- Secret scanning now produces fewer false positives for `slack_incoming_webhook_url`. ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-23-secret-scanning-reduces-false-positives-for-slack))
- Issue statuses and repository boards are in public preview. Assigning an agent to an issue, or linking a pull request to it, now changes the issue's status automatically. ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-23-issue-statuses-and-repository-boards-are-in-public-preview))
- Today's docs changes are terminology templating only. There is no substantive change.

### Action required
- **Coverage uploads must be Cobertura XML (effective now, no deadline given).** If a workflow step using `upload-code-coverage` starts failing with `This file is not a Cobertura XML report. Upload a Cobertura XML report.`, you have two options:
  - Configure your test framework to output Cobertura XML.
  - Convert the report to Cobertura XML before the upload step.

  Valid Cobertura reports are now processed more leniently. Minor structural issues no longer cause a rejection, and lines without a usable line number or hit count are skipped instead of discarding the whole report. This requires GitHub Code Quality to be enabled. It applies to GitHub Enterprise Cloud (including data residency) and GitHub Team, but not GitHub Enterprise Server. ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-23-code-coverage-uploads-now-flag-invalid-report-formats))

### Security improvements
- **Secret scanning, Slack:** The `slack_incoming_webhook_url` detector now excludes URLs that don't use Slack's incoming-webhook URL format. This should reduce alert noise. ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-23-secret-scanning-reduces-false-positives-for-slack))
- **Issue status automations (context for agent and automation governance):** This feature is in public preview and is not a security feature itself, but it changes what automations and agents can do with issues:
  - Agents and automations can read and set issue statuses through GraphQL, REST, and the MCP server.
  - Status changes can trigger Copilot automations.
  - Assigning an agent to an issue moves it to *In progress*.
  - Statuses stay in sync with matching GitHub Project status values.

  Teams that build automations on issue state should account for these new automatic transitions. ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-23-issue-statuses-and-repository-boards-are-in-public-preview))

### Docs changes worth reading
- Nothing substantive this time. One docs commit across the code-security pages ([#64801](https://github.com/github/docs/commit/528871b7d9904b5c16766e2d5bcab14c4a9a7fc6)) replaced hard-coded "AI Scan", "AI Scan for pull requests", and "AI Scan for repositories" names with product variables. Guidance, filters (e.g., `code-scanning-ai-scan-pr-scan`), and procedures are unchanged.

changelog.title: Issue statuses and repository boards are in public preview
changelog.text: Open or closed doesn’t always tell you where an issue stands. You can now use more specific statuses to give your team and agents shared context about what’s in flight and what to work on next, then visualize your progress with repository boards. Issue statuses Track progress directly on an issue. Choose a status when creating an issue or change it from the issue header. You’ll see it reflected in issue icons across the repository issues page, the issues dashboard , and repository boards, where you can use the status: filter to find the issues you’re looking for. Available statuses are: Backlog Todo In progress In review Done Not planned Duplicate Automated status updates. To help keep your statuses accurate, the following automations are applied to your issues: Linking a draft pull request to an issue moves the issue to In progress . Marking a draft pull request as Ready for review moves the issue to In review . Linking an open pull request to an issue moves the issue to In review . Assigning a user to an issue moves it to Todo . Assigning an agent to an issue moves it to In progress . If a GitHub Project has a status value that matches an issue status, changing either status updates the other. GraphQL, REST API, and MCP server support. Automations and agents can read an issue’s status, set a status, and choose an initial status when creating an issue. Status changes are also available as an automation trigger for Copilot automations. Repository boards Repository saved views now support a board layout, providing a quick way to see how work is progressing and update issues without leaving the repository. When you need more advanced planning features for your workflows, you can use a GitHub Project . Create a new view or open an existing view and switch to the board layout using the View options ⚙️ menu. Group by status to see your issues organized, and drag an issue to another column to update its status. Configure columns, swimlanes, visible fields, and sorting to customize your board. Issue fields are now independent of issue types Previously, issue fields other than Priority required mapping to an issue type to be shown on an issue. With this change, you can now add any issue field to an issue regardless of the type through the cog ⚙️ menu in the fields section of the issue sidebar. Fields will continue to only show by default if they have been pinned to a type. Learn more about issue fields in the documentation . Join the community discussion . The post Issue statuses and repository boards are in public preview appeared first on The GitHub Blog .

changelog.title: Secret scanning reduces false positives for Slack
changelog.text: Secret scanning now reduces false-positive detections for Slack secrets. False positives reduced The following detector improvements reduce false-positive matches for supported secrets. Provider Secret type Improvement Slack slack_incoming_webhook_url Exclude URLs that do not use Slack’s incoming-webhook URL format. Learn more Learn more about secret scanning and see the full list of supported secrets in our documentation. Let us know what you think in the community discussion . The post Secret scanning reduces false positives for Slack appeared first on The GitHub Blog .

changelog.title: Code coverage uploads now flag invalid report formats
changelog.text: The GitHub Code Quality upload-code-coverage action now checks that your coverage report is in Cobertura XML format. If it isn’t in a supported format, the upload step fails and the Actions log shows this error: This file is not a Cobertura XML report. Upload a Cobertura XML report. Previously, these uploads appeared to succeed, but no coverage showed up on your pull requests. Now you’ll find out about the problem in the workflow run, with a clear next step. If your workflow begins failing with this error, configure your test framework to output Cobertura XML, or convert your report to Cobertura XML before the upload step. We’ve also made processing more forgiving for valid Cobertura reports. We no longer reject a report because of minor structural issues, and we skip individual lines that don’t have a usable line number or hit count instead of discarding the whole report. To use code coverage, you need GitHub Code Quality enabled for your repository. This change is available now on GitHub Enterprise Cloud and GitHub Team, including GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency. It isn’t available on GitHub Enterprise Server. Learn more about setting up code coverage for your repository on GitHub Enterprise Cloud . The post Code coverage uploads now flag invalid report formats appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
